docs.message:
docs(pdt42): open counting instead of no tracking, platform as its own pitch

## Intent

Test trust already in the first draft, at the moment of decision: does the platform convince teachers on its own? Tracking means collecting data without the user's knowledge; counting single explicit interactions openly is something else, and it shows whether valuable use happens.

## Key changes

- The channels (D5) and KD-18: no hidden data collection. The platform counts explicit clicks openly ("I'll take a look", "used in class", thanks, structured feedback), stores only totals, uses no cookies or browser storage, and explains this at the button. The apps collect nothing.
- The channel "One place to find apps" has an entry through referral links. Each wave gets one code, never one per person, and the code is not stored in the browser.
- The first draft includes the teachers' experience and a riskiest trust assumption: the platform convinces teachers who do not know its initiator. At least 3 of them use an app and report it by click.
- The real MVP reaches teachers through forwarding, with the platform itself as the pitch and a short letter.
- The development plan updates KD-18, KD-19 and the next actions.

## Dependencies and side effects

- Hints remain for the criteria still open.

docs.message:
docs(pdt42): school-network criterion, parents tested later (D8)

## Intent

Settle two open points of the MVP, so that only the criteria that really need a value stay open.

## Key changes

- The school-network test succeeds if the anonymous thanks works at most of the schools of creators who teach. Block and prose say the same.
- Whether parents find the platform is tested only after the riskiest assumptions hold. Its missing test is accepted with a reason.

## Dependencies and side effects

- One hint remains: the criterion for running the platform alone.
